source: RECORDED from Claude Code CLI 2.1.322 via claude-agent-sdk 0.2.168 (claude-haiku-4-5), 2026-11-12; one run per scenario, throwaway cwd, existing login only. Not trimmed: every frame the CLI sent from the start to the end of the idle wait and of the follow-up turn is here in order, except thinking_tokens and rate-limit frames, thinking text and signatures, usage, and the shortening of ids and paths. failed_*: a background Bash `sleep 12; echo FAILMSG >&2; exit 3` ended while idle (the launch turn ended first); task_updated(failed) and task_notification(failed) were followed by an init and a CLI turn that answered it, ending in a Result with origin task-notification (runId = the task's run_id); the follow-up input 29 s later got a turn whose model knew the exit code, and no further notification. monitor_*: a Monitor (`echo tick-1; sleep 15`) woke the CLI once for its line (monitor_event: a turn with origin task-notification and no Task* frame), then ended by itself while idle: task_updated(completed), task_notification('stream ended'), then a CLI turn that answered it (origin task-notification with runId); the follow-up 29 s later got no further notification. stop_turn: the model stopped a background task itself with TaskStop inside its turn, so task_updated(killed) and task_notification(stopped) arrived with the turn open and no later turn followed in 34 s of idle; the follow-up turn answered from its own context. stop_idle_*: the same kind of task stopped through the SDK's stop_task while the session was idle (as close() does): task_updated(killed), task_notification(stopped), tasks_changed, then 32 s with no frame and no turn; the follow-up input's turn knew the task was stopped (the notification was carried into its context) and showed no notification frame of its own.

failed_launch.content: Run this as a background Bash command (run_in_background=true): sleep 12; echo FAILMSG >&2; exit 3. Then reply with only the word STARTED.

tool_result.content: Command running in background with ID: task-f. Output is being written to: /tasks/task-f.output

failed_report.summary: Background command "sleep 12; echo FAILMSG >&2; exit 3" failed with exit code 3

blocks.text: Background command completed with exit code 3 as expected.

failed_turn.result: Background command completed with exit code 3 as expected.

failed_followup.content: Without running any tool, answer in one short sentence: did any background task you started finish, and with what exit code?

blocks.text: Yes, the background task (task-f) finished with exit code 3.

failed_followup.result: Yes, the background task (task-f) finished with exit code 3.

monitor_launch.content: Use the Monitor tool to monitor the shell command: echo tick-1; sleep 15. After arming it, reply with only the word ARMED.

tool_result.content: Monitor started (task task-m, expires in 30s unless the source ends first; you get one notice at expiry).

monitor_report.summary: Monitor "monitoring shell command output" stream ended

blocks.text: Monitor completed. Command finished as expected after emitting "tick-1" and completing the 15-second sleep.

monitor_turn.result: Monitor completed. Command finished as expected after emitting "tick-1" and completing the 15-second sleep.

monitor_followup.content: Without running any tool, answer in one short sentence: did the monitor you armed end, and what did it report?

blocks.text: Yes, the monitor ended and reported the single event "tick-1".

monitor_followup.result: Yes, the monitor ended and reported the single event "tick-1".

stop_turn.content: Run 'sleep 120' as a background Bash command. In the next step stop that background task with the TaskStop tool. Then reply with only the word STOPPED.

tool_result.content: Command running in background with ID: task-s. Output is being written to: /tasks/task-s.output

stop_idle_launch.content: Run 'sleep 120' as a background Bash command, then reply with only the word STARTED.

tool_result.content: Command running in background with ID: task-i. Output is being written to: /tasks/task-i.output

stop_idle_followup.content: Without running any tool, answer in one short sentence: what happened to the background task you started?

blocks.text: The background sleep task was stopped by the user before it completed.

stop_idle_followup.result: The background sleep task was stopped by the user before it completed.
